research.stream: NVDA idiosyncratic overnight gap-downs: what happened next (non-earnings NVDA close-to-open <= -4% with QQQ close-to-open >= -0.5%, compared with all non-earnings NVDA gaps <= -4%)
key_findings: FREQUENCY. Purely company-specific gaps are rare. 2015-2026 has n=5 out of 2,931 non-earnings nights (0.17%). Dates are the night's close date: 2016-12-28, 2017-02-22, 2017-04-03, 2022-08-05 (pre-announcement), 2025-11-24. Only 2 fall after 2019. Extending back: 2005-2026 has n=12 (heuristic earnings flags before 2015) and 1999-2026 has n=19 (17 separate episodes). The extra pre-2015 dates are 1999-11-22, 2000-09-18, 2000-09-21, 2002-11-08, 2003-06-12, 2003-07-28, 2003-09-26, 2005-11-28, 2008-04-16, 2008-07-02, 2008-11-12, 2008-11-13, 2010-07-28 and 2013-08-09. For comparison, all non-earnings gaps <= -4% number 46 in 2015-2026 (31 episodes), 69 in 2005-2026 and 121 in 1999-2026. Every result for the company-specific set is tiny-n.

GAP DAY OPEN-TO-CLOSE. Company-specific gaps show no reliable rebound or follow-through. 2015-2026: +0.52% mean (n=5, bootstrap 95% CI -3.03 to +3.71, Welch t +0.23). 2005-2026: +0.82% (n=12). 1999-2026: +1.57% (n=19, t +1.2). All gaps <= -4% do rebound during the gap day: +1.66% (n=46, CI +0.29 to +3.07, t +2.2) and, for 1999-2026, +2.20% (n=121, t +3.5). The unconditional mean is about +0.08%.

NEXT OVERNIGHT (the hold from 15:52 today to 09:31 tomorrow; daily bars measure close to open). After company-specific gaps the point estimate is negative in every sample, but nothing is significant. 2015-2026: -1.06% (n=5, 1 of 5 positive, CI -2.76 to +0.65, t -1.16). 2005-2026: -0.59% (n=12, 4 of 12 positive, t -1.1). 1999-2026: -0.25% (n=19, 7 of 19 positive, t -0.7). The unconditional night averages +0.12% (sd 1.58, 56% positive). After all gaps <= -4% the next night is positive instead: 2015-2026 +0.63% (n=46, t +1.0; +0.16% when counted by episode); 1999-2026 +0.79% (n=121, CI +0.15 to +1.43, t +2.1). Gaps caused by the whole market partly reverse overnight; company-specific gaps did not.

NEXT-NIGHT TAIL. After company-specific gaps, a next overnight of -3% or worse occurred 2/5 (2015-2026), 3/12 (2005-2026) and 3/19 (1999-2026). The unconditional rates are 2.6%, 2.4% and 3.2% (binomial p 0.006, 0.003, 0.022), and the vol-matched baselines are 3.2%, 3.0% and 4.6%. This is the strongest company-specific result, but it is one of many metrics tested. The worst next nights were -4.03% (2008-11-12), -3.46% (2017-02-22) and -3.04% (2022-08-05). A next night of -5.1% or worse occurred 0/19 times (Wilson upper bound about 17%). Across all gaps <= -4% it occurred 1/46 in 2015-2026 (2024-08-02 to 08-05, -14.2%, a market-wide crash) and 4/121 in 1999-2026.

VOLATILITY. The next overnight moves about 1.7-1.8x as much as usual. Mean absolute move: 1.92% vs 1.06% (2015-2026, t 1.3) and 1.73% vs 0.99% (2005-2026, t 1.9). After all gaps <= -4% it is 2.2-2.4x (t 3.7 to 6.5). For a 2x ETF, variance on the night after the gap is roughly 3x normal.

SUM OF THE NEXT 5 AND 10 OVERNIGHTS (earnings nights set to 0, matching the account's rule). No reliable drift. Company-specific gaps: 2015-2026 +0.10% and -1.16% against unconditional +0.61% and +1.19% (sum10 t -2.0, but random-date p 0.25). 2005-2026: +0.16% and +0.61% against +0.45% and +0.87%. 1999-2026: +1.17% and +2.09% against +0.47% and +0.90%. All gaps <= -4%, 2015-2026: +0.95% and +1.24% against +0.61% and +1.19% (t 0.3 and 0.0).

FURTHER CRASH WITHIN 10 NIGHTS (another non-earnings overnight <= -5%). Company-specific gaps were not followed by more crashes: 0/5 (2015-2026), 0/12 (2005-2026) and 2/19 (1999-2026; both hits are 2000-2002, one of them near a heuristic earnings date). Unconditional rates are 4.9%, 4.3% and 7.6%; vol-matched rates are 4.6%, 5.8% and 11.7%. The Wilson upper bounds are wide (43%, 24% and 31%), so a raised risk cannot be ruled out. All gaps <= -4% cluster strongly: 12/46 = 26% (Wilson 16-40%) against 4.9% (p<0.001), 5/31 = 16% by episode (p 0.016), and 36/121 = 30% in 1999-2026 against 7.6%. Those clusters come from market regimes (COVID Feb-Mar 2020, DeepSeek Jan 2025, tariffs Apr 2025), not company news.

CAUSES AND THE POST-HOC NEWS SET. Causes I verified: 2017-02-22 Nomura downgrade; 2017-04-03 Pacific Crest downgrade; 2019-01-25 revenue pre-announcement; 2022-08-05 pre-announcement; 2022-08-31 China export licence (8-K); 2023-10-16 US export rules; 2025-04-15 H20 charge; 2025-11-24 Meta/Google TPU report; 2008-07-02 revenue warning plus faulty-chip charge. Four of these fail the QQQ >= -0.5% filter because NVDA's own weight and its peers dragged QQQ down. Together the 8 dated 2015-2026 (selected after the fact) give: next overnight -1.05% (6 of 8 negative, CI -2.35 to +0.33, t -1.6); gap-day open-to-close -0.60%; sum of 5 nights +0.95%; sum of 10 nights -1.07% (6 of 8 negative, t -2.2); further crash 0/8. The three US/China export-policy nights give a next overnight of +1.17%, -3.07% and -0.04%. NVDA has no history of a CEO, key-person or counter-intelligence event, so there is no direct analog.

WHAT THE DATA SAYS OVERALL. After a company-specific gap, NVDA's usual overnight edge does not show up: the next nights are flat to slightly negative, more volatile, and more often -3% or worse, but they did not lead into a run of crashes. After market-wide gaps the next night tends to rebound, while further -5% nights cluster (26-30% within 10 nights).

MULTIPLE COMPARISONS. I tested 6 definitions x 5 samples x more than 10 metrics. The only company-specific results below p 0.05 are the tail rate for a next night <= -3% and the post-hoc news set's sum10. Treat both as hypotheses, not findings.

THE QQQ FILTER IS IMPERFECT. NVDA is a large QQQ weight (the exact weight is UNVERIFIED; I assumed about 8-10%) and moves its peers, so its own news drags QQQ down. The QQQ >= -0.5% rule therefore drops real company-specific nights such as 2019-01-25, 2022-08-31, 2023-10-16 and 2025-04-15. The news-tagged set fixes this but is chosen after the fact.

EARNINGS FLAGS BEFORE 2015 ARE HEURISTIC. They come from the volume-ratio method (38/47 exact on 2015-2026). Three of the 19 company-specific events from 1999-2026 (1999-11-22, 2002-11-08, 2013-08-09) are within 3 sessions of a heuristic date and may be earnings-related. The conservative 2005-2026 variant without them gives n=11 and a next overnight of -0.65%.
The 1999-2004 period (dot-com era, high volatility) supplies the only 2 further-crash hits and raises the baselines. Results that include it are less relevant to today.
Random-date Monte Carlo p-values understate the uncertainty in means, because nights after a gap have 1.5-2x normal variance. Rely on the Welch t-stats and bootstrap CIs.

NO ANALOG. NVDA has no historical CEO, key-person or counter-intelligence governance event. The historical events are mostly one-shot news (downgrades, pre-announcements, export rules). A board review that is still open can produce more headlines at any hour, including overnight. That is my judgment and is not captured in the base rates.

research.implication_for_overnight_holding:
History argues against reading today's gap as either a buy-the-dip night or the start of a crash run, and it does not show the usual positive overnight edge. Read it as a weak signal with higher-than-normal variance.

After company-specific NVDA gaps, the next overnight (tonight's analog, Monday to Tuesday) averaged -0.25% to -1.06% across samples, against +0.1% normally. None of these t-stats exceed 1.2 in magnitude, and the n is 5 to 19. The planning edge of +0.30%/night is not present on these nights.

Next-night volatility runs about 1.7x normal. A move of -3% or worse in NVDA (about -6% on NVDL) occurred 2/5, 3/12 and 3/19 times, against about 3% normally. A move of -5% or worse never occurred (0/19), but the 95% upper bound is about 17%.

Over 5 to 10 nights there was no reliable drift. Another -5% gap within 10 nights did not follow any company-specific gap after 2002 (0/12 in 2005-2026). Market-wide gaps are different: they cluster (26-30%), but they also rebound on the next night.

For this account, if my approximate derivation holds, a further NVDA overnight of about -5% from the ~176.9 level would reach PAUSE. History puts that at roughly a 0-17% chance, with a point estimate near the low end. More likely is a -3% night costing about 6% of equity. Even the historical sample's average outcome is slightly negative.

Holding at normal size tonight is therefore not supported by an edge. The downside is not historically catastrophic either. If the rules allow discretion, PAUSE-style sizing (1 share) or sitting out for 1 to 2 nights is a reasonable risk trade-off. The cost is about one night's expected edge (~0.3% gross per unit of exposure), and this evidence does not meet the repo's pre-registration bar (t >= 2) for a rule change.

The base rates cannot price the board review itself: it is an ongoing key-person and governance story with possible overnight headlines, and NVDA has no precedent for one.

research.stream: CEO governance/scandal/security shock case studies (second-gap frequency, paths, resolution time)
key_findings: Sample: 15 cases measured with Robinhood daily bars (HPQ/Hurd 2010, WYNN 2018, META/Cambridge Analytica 2018, INTC/Krzanich 2018, JD/Liu 2018, TSLA/Musk SEC 2018, SMCI 'Big Hack' 2018, BA/Muilenburg 2019, MCD/Easterbrook 2019, BABA/Jack Ma 2020, ERIC Iraq-ISIS 2022, BP/Looney 2023, MSFT via OpenAI/Altman 2023, SMCI Hindenburg/10-K/EY 2024, INTC/Lip-Bu Tan 2025). CBS/Moonves, ATVI/Kotick and Uber/Kalanick are documented from web sources only, because Robinhood has no bars for them (CBS and ATVI) or the company was private (Uber).

The split that matters most is whether the CEO was still in place after the first shock. Where the exit was announced with the news (HPQ, INTC18, MCD, BP), there was no second move of 5% or more in the next 10 sessions (0/4), and 20-day paths were flat to modestly negative. Where the CEO stayed, 8/11 had a second move of 5% or more, against about 4.1 expected from each stock's own base rate.

Adverse overnight gaps of 5% or more after the shock day occurred in 4/15 cases (WYNN -5.0%, JD -5.1%, ERIC -6.6%, SMCI24 -11.3%). In all four, the first one came on the very next overnight, driven by a new revelation or escalation (regulators and the RNC exit over the weekend, the police report, continued selling in Stockholm, the 10-K delay).

A single overnight gap of -9.8% or worse within 2 weeks happened in only 2/15 cases: SMCI24 (-11.3% on the 10-K delay) and ERIC (-14.2% on the DOJ finding that it breached its plea deal). Both were sub-$100B names facing hard legal or accounting catalysts.

Size and type matter. Among names of roughly $100B or more at the time (HPQ, META, INTC18, BA, MCD, BABA, MSFT, BP; caps approximate), none had an overnight gap of 5% or more in the 10 sessions after the shock (0/8). Only BABA had a 5%+ close-to-close day (-8.3% on draft anti-monopoly rules; its open was only -3.6%). The large-cap cases where the CEO stayed (META, BA, BABA, MSFT) had worst overnights of -1.4% to -3.6%, but META and BABA still drifted about -10% over 10 sessions through a series of 2-4% down days.

For an overnight-only holder starting at the shock-day close, the median return over the next 10 overnights was -1.0% at 1x and -2.0% for a 2x daily-reset proxy. The range was enormous: ERIC -56.9% and SMCI24 -36.8% on the downside, TSLA +47.4%, SMCI18 +57.9% and INTC25 +22.0% on the upside. META lost 14.8% at 2x overnight-only with no single gap of 5% or more.

Resolution events usually gapped UP: 9/10 were positive, with a median of about +5.6%. Examples: WYNN +8.6% on the CEO's resignation, TSLA +17.3% on the SEC settlement, JD +5.9% when no charges were filed, SMCI +28.7% when the special committee found no misconduct, INTC25 +5.6% after the Trump meeting, BABA +5.5% when Ma reappeared, META +4.5% on testimony day, BA +2.9% on the firing, MSFT +2.05%. CBS was the exception at -1.5%. Adverse second gaps came from new escalations (regulators, DOJ, auditors, filings, state action), not from resolutions.

Resolution time is bimodal. When an outside party can end it (SEC settlement, a partner, the President), it took 2-5 days: TSLA 1 session, MSFT/Altman 1 session to the hire and about 5 days to reinstatement, INTC25 3 sessions to the White House meeting. Board-run or legal reviews took weeks to months: CEO exit after 11 days at WYNN, 44 days at CBS, 66 days at BA and about 4 months at Uber; formal findings after about 3 months at SMCI (12/2/2024) and about 4.7 months at CBS (12/17/2018); legal clearance after about 16 weeks at JD. The median across 9 cases where the CEO stayed and a resolution date is defined is 15 sessions.

NVDA mapping: the first leg of this story, the NYT report of 2026-10-29, had almost no NVDA-specific move (10/29 NVDA -0.8% vs QQQ -1.4%; 10/30 -4.2% vs -3.5%). Today's premarket move (about -5.2% vs QQQ +0.75%, so roughly -6% relative) is an escalation: a board-run independent review plus Huang's admission. That puts NVDA in the open-ended, CEO-stays bucket, but as a mega-cap. That is a combination where the analogs show drift risk more than single-night gap risk.

No precise precedent exists for a mega-cap CEO reportedly targeted by a foreign-intelligence (MSS) effort. The nearest national-security analogs: INTC/Lip-Bu Tan 2025 (China ties; the President turned supportive within 4 days and every 5%+ move in the first 8 sessions was UP); ERIC 2022 (terror financing, a cascade of large down gaps); SMCI 2018 (spy-chip allegation, -41% and then denials backed by DHS/NCSC; small cap). Here Trump backed Huang from the start, which looks more like the INTC25 de-escalation path.

caveats: Small and mixed sample (n=15 with data). Shock types range from personal conduct to regulatory, legal, short-seller and national-security cases. Famous cases are partly famous because they moved, so there is selection bias.

Market confounders: WYNN's window overlaps the Feb 2018 volatility spike; ERIC's overlaps the Russian invasion (2/24/2022), so its 2/28 -9% gap is not purely the scandal; JD's overlaps the US-China tariff escalation (Sept 2018); TSLA and SMCI 2018 overlap the October 2018 selloff.
ERIC and BP 'overnight gaps' are US ADR gaps that include the Stockholm and London primary sessions. That inflates ERIC's gap counts relative to a US-primary stock like NVDA.
WYNN, BA and MSFT news broke intraday, so their T0 shock shows up as an intraday move and the gap metrics are not strictly comparable to NVDA's premarket shock.

Base rates use the prior up-to-250 sessions; for WYNN only 94 sessions were available (from Sep 2017), so its base rate of 0 is unreliable. SMCI 2024 (0.94) and INTC 2025 (0.79) already had very high base volatility.

Market-cap buckets (roughly $100B or more vs less) are approximate and UNVERIFIED; caps were not pulled from a data tool. Being open-ended and being small-cap overlap: every sub-$100B case was open-ended.
Daily RTH bars only. No extended-hours or intraday analog data, so 'overnight' means RTH close to next RTH open and does not reproduce the 15:52-09:31 hold exactly.
No price data for CBS 2018 or ATVI 2021 (not in Robinhood), so whether they had a second gap within 2 weeks is UNVERIFIED. Uber and OpenAI were private.

UNVERIFIED items: cause of INTC's +5.4% gap on 2025-08-19 (believed SoftBank investment, not checked); cause of META's -4.9% on 2018-03-27; the reported House request for Huang to appear in a private session on Nov 18 (it came from a search-result summary; the CNBC article does not mention it); exact CBS close on 2018-07-27 (sources say about -6%).
The 2x overnight-only figures are a daily-reset proxy (1 + 2 x each overnight return), not actual NVDL fills; they ignore fees and tracking error.

There is no historical precedent of a mega-cap CEO tied to a foreign-intelligence (MSS) targeting report. The national-security analogs (INTC/Tan, ERIC, SMCI 2018) differ materially in mechanism and size.

research.implication_for_overnight_holding:
These cases suggest the highest-risk point is the first one or two overnights after an escalation, not the shock itself. Where the CEO stayed in place, 4 of 11 cases had an adverse overnight gap of -5% or worse, and in each the first one came on the very next night, driven by fresh news (regulators, a police report, a 10-K delay, DOJ action).

NVDA should be read against the mega-cap subset. None of the 8 names worth roughly $100B or more had any overnight gap of 5% or more in the following 2 weeks. A -9.8% or worse single night occurred in only 2 of 15 cases, both smaller companies facing filing, auditor or DOJ catalysts, with no mega-cap analog. NVDA's own base rate for a -5% or worse non-earnings overnight is about 0.6% per night, with none in the last 246 nights. My judgment, not a measured probability: the risk of a -5% NVDA night (about -10% NVDL) over the next few nights is several times normal but probably still well under 1 in 3. A -9.8% single night remains a tail scenario.

The larger documented risk for a 2x overnight-only holder is drift through repeated -2% to -4% opens without any big gap. META in 2018 lost 14.8% over 10 nights on a 2x overnight-only basis with no gap of 5% or more; BABA's 10-session close-to-close path was about -10%. With equity near the pause level, that cumulative bleed matters as much as a single gap.

If the pause is measured against Friday's close of 186.64, the remaining cushion from the 176.9 premarket is about -4.8%. In 5 of 12 cases where the news broke before the open, the stock was at least that much lower at the next day's open (raw, not market-adjusted), and in 9 of 12 at some open within 10 sessions.

Offsetting factors:
- Resolution and de-escalation events usually gapped up (9 of 10 positive, median about +5.6%), so the second large gap is two-sided for a long holder.
- Trump's early support resembles the Intel/Lip-Bu Tan 2025 de-escalation path.
- Board-run reviews typically take 6 weeks to 5 months, so the review is unlikely to resolve before the Nov 17 earnings night unless Huang exits.

Watch for fresh revelations: new NYT or FT reporting, government or congressional action (the Nov 18 congressional session is UNVERIFIED), or board findings. In the analogs, events like these, rather than the original shock, produced the adverse second gaps.

Event split model: total variance = base variance per trading day x trading days + earnings-day variance. Weekends are folded into Monday's day, and base vol is assumed constant over the window. If the 11/13 base includes post-crash or headline vol that the market expected to decay, method A understates the earnings variance. Both methods give 8.2-8.8%.

Historical IV uses daily last-trade option closes, which are asynchronous with the stock close and are not mids. ATM is interpolated from OTM options only. Spot sat slightly outside the fetched strikes on 10/19-10/21 and 10/26-10/28 (flat extrapolation). The base-vol history subtracts Friday's earnings variance, assuming it was constant through the window.

Overnight sigma = implied per-trading-day sigma x sqrt(overnight share). The share comes from 1-2 years of RTH open/close bars. In a headline-driven week more variance may arrive overnight (the last 20 nights show 0.43), hence the 0.60 stress row. NVDL is modelled as 2.0x NVDA close-to-open; the empirical beta is 1.97. The 15:52-16:00 and 09:30-09:31 slivers, premarket spreads and NVDL tracking or fees are ignored.

Tail models: t3 and t4 are scaled to the same variance as the normal. 'empz' standardizes 2015-2026 overnights by a lagged trailing-20 realized sd. That inflates tails in regime shifts relative to an implied-sigma forecast, so read it as an upper reference. # NVDL hold: decision memo (Mon 9 Nov, ~08:30 ET)

## 1. What happened
Confirmed: on Sunday Nvidia's board opened an independent review of Jensen Huang. It set no timeline and has "confidence in Jensen" [1]. Huang admitted an affair and remains CEO. Trump backs him, and China calls the story "smears" [2]. House chairs have requested, not subpoenaed, a briefing from him on Nov 18 [3]. There is no 8-K filing yet [4]. At 08:21, NVDA was down 5.5% and QQQ up 0.7%, so the move is Nvidia-only.
Reported only, from anonymous sources: a US memo says the woman was recruited by Chinese intelligence [2][5].

## 2. Extra risk before earnings
Six held nights remain. The 11/17 earnings night is already in cash [6].
- Friday's options, priced before the news, implied about ±2-2.4% per NVDA night. That is ±4-5% a night for NVDL and ±11-13% over six nights. Live volatility is probably higher.
- Chance over six nights of an NVDA night of -5% or worse: 10-25%. Of -9.8% or worse: 1-5%.
- History: after 19 Nvidia-only gaps since 1999, the next night averaged -0.25% to -1.06%, against +0.12% normally. Not statistically reliable. Swings ran 1.8x normal; no crash runs followed after 2005.
- In 15 CEO-scandal cases [7], slow bleed was the commonest harm: a 2x overnight loss of 10%+ within 10 nights hit 6, against a normal 8-15%. Board reviews take weeks to months [8].
- After this morning's exit, the PAUSE cushion is roughly a 9-10% cumulative NVDL fall. Approximate; recompute from the account.
- My rough simulation (UNVERIFIED) puts the chance of hitting PAUSE before earnings at 19-33%, or 40-48% under stress.

## 3. Options
(a) Keep the rules. Expected gain +1.1-1.6% of equity if the planning edge holds (past gaps like this showed none). PAUSE chance is 19-33%. PAUSE then means 1 share for 5 sessions.
(b) Hold cash until 11/18 15:52. Forgoes about $1 (1.1-1.6%) and removes this risk. But the House date and the Shenzhen APEC summit fall on 11/18-19 [9], and the review could take months.
(c) Trade smaller, in whole shares; one NVDL share is about 25% of equity. Two shares forgo 0.5-0.7% with a 5-11% PAUSE chance. One share forgoes 0.8-1.2% with under 1% PAUSE chance. Both are rule changes: PAUSE only acts at 80% of the 20-session high.

## 4. Recommendation
Keep (a). Evidence of extra harm is weak. §6 accepts single-stock gap risk, and PAUSE is the built-in brake. §3(g) forbids rule changes on drawdowns, so the agent cannot deviate on its own.
If a roughly 1-in-4 PAUSE risk is too much, choose (c) at 2 shares for these six nights, costing about 50 cents in expectation. Give an explicit instruction or a dated rule amendment before 15:48. If live 11/13 option volatility is above about 70% after 09:45, I lean to (c).
